sections.heading: Professional summary
sections.content: Aditya More is a Data Scientist and Machine Learning Engineer with an M.S. in Computer Science from Clemson University. He builds end-to-end data science and machine learning systems, from data preprocessing and model development through evaluation and deployment. His interests include machine learning, deep learning, large language models, computer vision, AI security, MLOps, and retrieval-augmented generation.

sections.heading: Career goals and availability
sections.content: Aditya is based in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and is willing to relocate within the United States. He is open to AI Engineer, Machine Learning Engineer, and Data Scientist roles. He is authorized to work in the United States under OPT and does not require immediate sponsorship.

sections.heading: Languages
sections.content: Aditya speaks English professionally and is a native or bilingual speaker of Hindi and Marathi.

sections.heading: Researcher - LLM Agents and Human Behavior at Clemson University
sections.content: Aditya has served as a Researcher in Clemson University's School of Computing from April 2026 to the present, working remotely. Under the supervision of Dr. Long Cheng, he investigates whether societies of Large Language Model agents can realistically simulate human behavior and support early-stage behavioral studies. He reproduces published behavioral experiments and designs new studies with AgentSociety, YuLan-OneSim, Generative Agents, MiroFish, and related multi-agent frameworks. He is developing a taxonomy and metrics for behavioral realism, consistency, and human alignment across decision-making, social interaction, cooperation, trust, and other behavioral dimensions. The work includes Trust Game and Dictator Game experiments that compare LLM-agent decisions with established human behavioral data, and a broader assessment of whether AI agents can support or partially substitute human participants in behavioral pilot studies. Technologies and research tools include Python, Large Language Models, Multi-Agent Systems, literature review, experimental design, and behavioral evaluation.

sections.heading: Graduate Teaching Assistant — Clemson University
sections.content: Aditya worked as a Graduate Teaching Assistant for Applied Data Science in Clemson University's School of Computing from August 2024 through December 2025. He designed Jupyter labs and assignments covering data preprocessing, supervised learning, unsupervised learning, model evaluation, and visualization. He built automated grading pipelines with Python and nbgrader to reduce manual effort and improve scoring consistency, maintained live course infrastructure, resolved notebook and autograder issues, and explained machine-learning concepts while debugging student code during office hours. He also collaborated with faculty on curriculum design and Coursera deployment. Technologies included Python, Jupyter, scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy, nbgrader, and Coursera.

sections.heading: Software Test Engineer — Amdocs
sections.content: Aditya worked as a Software Test Engineer at Amdocs in Pune, India, from October 2021 through December 2022. He performed end-to-end, regression, and integration testing for enterprise telecom systems supporting AT&T; designed test cases and validation strategies from product requirements and stakeholder input; and ran functional, UI, and API release tests with Selenium and Postman. He triaged defects with cross-functional Agile teams in the United States and India and participated in requirements analysis and production-release validation.

sections.heading: M.S. Computer Science — Clemson University
sections.content: Aditya earned a Master of Science in Computer Science from Clemson University in Clemson, South Carolina. He attended from January 2024 through December 2025, graduated in December 2025, concentrated in Data Science and Informatics, and earned a 3.7/4.0 GPA. Coursework included AI-Receptive Software Development, Applied Data Science, Cloud Computing Architecture, Database Management Systems, Deep Learning, Design and Analysis of Algorithms, Machine Learning Implementation and Evaluation, Security in Emerging Systems, and Statistical Methods I. His academic work included ML and deep-learning models, data pipelines, model evaluation, LLM robustness, AI defense mechanisms, and statistical analysis.

sections.heading: B.E. Computer Science and Engineering — D.Y. Patil
sections.content: Aditya earned a Bachelor of Engineering in Computer Science and Engineering from D.Y. Patil College of Engineering & Technology in Kolhapur, India. He attended from August 2017 through July 2021 and earned a 3.22/4.0 GPA. Coursework included Data Structures, C and C++ programming labs, Data Analytics, Operating Systems, Advanced Database Systems, and Internet of Things. He led a five-member team that built an automatic license plate recognition system and a real-time COVID-19 safety monitoring system.

sections.heading: Certifications
sections.content: Aditya's listed credentials include Data Science Orientation from IBM, IBM Blockchain Essentials V2, Cybersecurity Fundamentals from IBM, Build Your Own Chatbot — Level 1 from IBM, Introduction to Cybersecurity from Cisco, Certified Information Security and Ethical Hacker (CISEH), and Programming in C and C++. Clemson University awarded his Master of Science in Computer Science in December 2025.

sections.heading: BB8 Co-Pilot x Tech Portfolio — RAG architecture
sections.content: BB-8 is the active RAG-powered co-pilot for Aditya's Tech Portfolio. It uses the OpenAI Responses API and OpenAI embeddings with retrieval-augmented generation over structured, verified portfolio knowledge. Amazon S3 Vectors provides semantic retrieval, while a deterministic local keyword retriever provides an availability fallback. BB-8 retrieves relevant chunks, grounds the model with only that evidence, and returns source-page links.

sections.heading: BB8 Co-Pilot x Tech Portfolio — agent capabilities and operations
sections.content: The live BB-8 co-pilot preserves chat state while navigating, offers the current resume, and prepares contact-form drafts for visitor review without sending them. The Next.js and TypeScript application includes retrieval evaluation, OpenAI usage telemetry, privacy-aware first-party analytics, DynamoDB-backed content administration, and AWS Amplify SSR deployment. Source: https://github.com/Skywalker1910/Tech-Portfolio. Live system: https://www.adityamore.dev.

sections.heading: BB8 Co-Pilot x Tech Portfolio versus BB-8: Transformer Language Model
sections.content: BB-8: Transformer Language Model is a separate LLM engineering study and does not serve or power the live portfolio assistant. BB8 Co-Pilot x Tech Portfolio uses OpenAI models plus portfolio RAG; the research project implements and evaluates Transformer language models from scratch.

sections.heading: Movie Recommendation Engine — data and baseline results
sections.content: Aditya expanded a 2024 Clemson course project into a live full-stack movie recommendation product. The reproducible study combines MovieLens, TMDB, and IMDb data with FunkSVD, NeuMF, TF-IDF content similarity, and Bayesian popularity. It processed more than 26 million ratings across 270,000 users and 45,000 movies. FunkSVD achieved RMSE 0.7600, about 21 percent better than the baseline.

sections.heading: Movie Recommendation Engine — NeuMF v2 improvements
sections.content: In September 2026, NeuMF v2 improved validation RMSE from 1.0725 to 0.8543, improved MAE from 0.8078 to 0.6452, and reduced parameters from 26.3 million to 13.1 million. Versioned model artifacts live at https://huggingface.co/Skywalker1910/movie-rec-models and download automatically when absent.

sections.heading: Movie Recommendation Engine — product and deployment
sections.content: The application provides personalized onboarding, watch history, live TMDB enrichment, an isolated admin dashboard, model diagnostics, and lazy model loading. Flask, React, SQLite, Docker, nginx, gunicorn, SSL, and GitHub Actions deploy the service to AWS EC2. Source: https://github.com/Skywalker1910/Movies-Recommendation-Engine. Live system: https://movies.adityamore.dev.

sections.heading: Skynet — AQI Prediction System
sections.content: Completed in 2025, Skynet is an end-to-end machine-learning pipeline for forecasting Air Quality Index. It integrated NASA TEMPO, OpenAQ, weather, and traffic APIs; implemented ingestion and preprocessing pipelines; engineered environmental and traffic features; and modeled temporal and spatial AQI patterns. Technologies included Python, scikit-learn, pandas, and NumPy.

sections.heading: BB-8: Transformer Language Model — architecture and experiment progression
sections.content: BB8 is Aditya's 2026 graduate-level LLM engineering project, separate from the live BB-8 portfolio co-pilot. He implemented a decoder-only GPT-style Transformer in PyTorch from first principles: embeddings, learned positional embeddings, scaled dot-product attention, multi-head attention, GELU feed-forward layers, Pre-LN decoder blocks, causal masking, character, word, and BPE tokenizers, training and evaluation loops, and decoding strategies. Across 11 documented experiments, the project progressed from 112,320-parameter character models through BPE models, Qwen2.5-0.5B LoRA fine-tuning, and grounded retrieval with citations and abstention.

sections.heading: BB-8: Transformer Language Model — chat evaluation findings
sections.content: An 80-case, five-configuration chat evaluation suite traced failures to a prompt-format mismatch and a preprocessing bug that truncated 29 percent of training examples. An 88-case grounded-QA benchmark with an 80 percent promotion gate rejected a model with perplexity 1.03 because it passed only 22 percent of content and citation checks.

sections.heading: BB-8: Transformer Language Model — reproducibility and deployment
sections.content: After detecting a tokenizer data leak, Aditya added dataset hashing, commit pinning, versioned configurations, and a model registry. The project includes an interactive Token Lab, Hugging Face artifacts, and a CPU AWS Lambda and API Gateway deployment path. Source: https://github.com/Skywalker1910/BB-8. Live application: https://chat.adityamore.dev/. Model artifacts: https://huggingface.co/Skywalker1910/BB8.

sections.heading: Adversarial Attacks — Experimentation and Case Study
sections.content: This 2024 Clemson AI-security case study examined data poisoning, adversarial patches, and evasion attacks on computer-vision models. Aditya experimented with monocular depth-estimation systems used in autonomous-vehicle perception, analyzed effects on scene understanding and depth pipelines, and evaluated attack transferability across models and threat settings. Technologies and areas included Python, computer vision, deep learning, adversarial machine learning, and AI security.

sections.heading: LLM Jailbreak Defense Evaluation
sections.content: During Spring 2025 in Clemson's CPSC 8570 security course, Aditya and his team replicated and extended the MASTERKEY jailbreak framework for black-box evaluation of commercial LLMs. They built a 13-category dataset from public jailbreak sources and custom augmentations, automated prompt execution and result logging, calculated query-success rates, and categorized timeouts, exceptions, and AI refusals. The evaluation also tracked latency and token usage without requiring internal model access. Source: https://github.com/Skywalker1910/Evaluating-Defense-Mechanisms-Jailbreak-LLMs.

sections.heading: Deep Learning Coursework — video captioning and spoken question answering
sections.content: Aditya's four-repository CPSC 8430 graduate coursework implemented deep-learning systems end to end in Python and PyTorch. He built an attention-based Seq2Seq encoder-decoder for video captioning with BLEU evaluation and fine-tuned BERT-Base for question answering on Spoken-SQuAD using document stride, automatic mixed precision, gradient checkpointing, and gradient accumulation. The Spoken-SQuAD assignment reported 63.5 percent F1 and 40.1 percent exact match.

sections.heading: Deep Learning Coursework — GAN variants
sections.content: For the generative-model assignment, Aditya implemented DCGAN, WGAN, and ACGAN image-generation variants and evaluated them with Frechet Inception Distance and Inception Score. The CPSC 8430 repositories are grouped at https://github.com/Skywalker1910?tab=repositories&q=CPSC-8430.

sections.heading: Neural Log — Personal Activity and Progress System
sections.content: Neural Log is Aditya's live 2026 personal activity system for training, nutrition, learning, habits, goals, and long-term progress. It uses eight evidence-based attributes and an auditable XP transaction ledger, along with records, streaks, calendar heatmaps, analytics, privacy-aware leaderboards, private AI weekly reviews, and illustrated personal libraries. Its September 2026 releases added admin-managed invite codes, isolated administration, polished responsive workspaces, and tested nutrition-label auto-capture. Flask serves a React and TypeScript frontend from one origin, SQLite is authoritative, and numbered SQL migrations, verified backups, and automated tests support operation. Docker Compose runs Flask and Gunicorn behind Caddy on AWS Lightsail. Source: https://github.com/Skywalker1910/Neural-Log. Live system: https://neurallog.adityamore.dev.

sections.heading: FIFA World Cup 2026 Prediction Platform
sections.content: Aditya built a live, SQLite-backed World Cup prediction platform for a private group. A dependency-free Node HTTP server serves distinct US and India scoring experiences from one deployment, with authenticated player and AI-agent accounts, prediction locking, score forecasts, public picks, profiles, leaderboards, group tables, best-third-place projections, and a road-to-final bracket. Its private Command Center manages accounts, official results, prediction records, settings, regional ledgers, score synchronization, and audit history. The containerized service runs on Railway with persistent storage. Source: https://github.com/Skywalker1910/FIFA-World-Cup-2026. Live system: https://game.adityamore.dev.

sections.heading: FIFA 2026 AI Prediction Agents — prediction workflow
sections.content: Aditya built a companion Node service whose LLM agents authenticate as dedicated player accounts, read eligible live fixtures, and submit structured winner and score predictions with rationale, confidence, provider, model, response ID, and token metadata. The OpenAI implementation validates teams, match IDs, lock windows, and output structure.

sections.heading: FIFA 2026 AI Prediction Agents — automation and providers
sections.content: The prediction agent supports dry-run, due-window, next-match, and update-existing modes, retries transient database locks, and can run automatically every ten minutes on a GitHub Actions schedule. Claude and Gemini adapters are scaffolded for later providers. Source: https://github.com/Skywalker1910/FIFA-World-Cup-2026-AI-Agents.
